topic: Graph search planners: grids, Dijkstra, A* and heuristics
title: Plan a path across the warehouse floor
instructions:
## A delivery robot on an occupancy grid

A warehouse robot has mapped the floor as an occupancy grid: dark cells are shelving, S is the robot and G is the loading bay. It moves one cell up, down, left or right per step.

## Do this

1. Run **Breadth-first search**. It expands cells in rings around S and finds a shortest path, but it does not know where G is.
2. Run **A* on a grid**, which adds the Manhattan distance to G as its estimate. Compare the number of cells each expands.
hints: The path length is the number of moves, one less than the number of cells on the path.
BFS reports the expanded count when it removes G from the queue.
On an open floor, Manhattan distance is exact until the robot meets the shelves, so A* heads almost straight there.
